points.description: Recognises that with buffer size N = 10, the system has fewer than 10 packets except when it is full (exactly 10 packets), so the answer needs the blocking/full-state probability P_B (or equivalently P(X<10) = 1 − P_B, or a sum of state probabilities 0..9).
Calculates the probability using the M/M/1/N formula with utilization ρ = 9/10 = 0.9: P_B = ((1−ρ)ρ^N)/(1−ρ^(N+1)) ≈ 0.0508, so P(X<10) ≈ 0.949.
points.partial_credit: Half if the correct formula or approach is stated but the numeric value is wrong or missing.

points.description: Multiplies the 60 s observation time by P(X<10) = 1 − P_B to get the expected time, about 56.95 seconds (≈57 s).
points.partial_credit: Half if the multiplication by 60 is shown with a wrong probability.

rubric.notes: Full marks need the full-buffer (blocking) reasoning, the M/M/1/N probability with ρ = 0.9, and the final step of multiplying by 60 to get about 56.95 s. Give part marks for a correct method with a numerical slip or a missing value. Give no marks for a bare number with no justification, or for M/M/1 without a finite buffer. Marks are awarded in quarter steps overall, so round the total to the nearest 0.25.
